feature_title: Azure SQL bronze ingestion via Dataflow Gen2 (bronze_azureSQLdb2table)
rationale: The last RefreshDataflow in the orchestrator pipeline, and the only item a service principal cannot run. It failed on two independent, recurring axes after CI/CD landed: (1) every `fabric-cicd` publish STRIPS Dataflow Gen2 connection credentials, because they live outside the git definition, leaving the item deployed-but-unbound; (2) once re-bound by hand, an SPN-triggered refresh fails outright with `SPNBasedRefreshNotAllowed` (dataflow id 47f7a4ab-2b69-4275-8171-1f6bd55b25e4). Both re-break `bronze_procurement` on EVERY automated deploy, so this blocked DEC-007's push-to-main flip and not merely task-046. Replaced by Copy activities reading Azure SQL directly, which store their credential in Fabric's own connection store — the pattern already proven green under the SPN by `bronzecopy_EUSupplyShares` and `bronzecopy_GlobalSupplyShares`. A PySpark notebook (the task-035 pattern used for EPI/WGI) was considered and rejected: those sources are public HTTP with no secret, whereas Azure SQL needs a credential at runtime and the repo has no JDBC or secret-retrieval pattern. Key Vault was ruled out as a secret source for an in-notebook connection: it would need cross-tenant-style credential plumbing this project has no pattern for, and no JDBC or secret-retrieval code exists anywhere in the repo (probed with a positive control). NOTE: the original rationale said Fabric and the Azure subscription were in DIFFERENT tenants — that was WRONG, and was corrected on 2026-07-31. Both live in tenant a7d750d0; there are simply two az accounts, and only the tenant-level fabricuser@erikemilssonhotmail.onmicrosoft.com has Fabric access. The decision to use a Copy activity stands on its own merits (credential in Fabric's connection store, SPN-safe, survives publish) and does not depend on the mistaken tenant claim. Mechanism chosen by Erik 2026-07-31; full reasoning in task-048 notes.
restore_notes:
READ THIS BEFORE RESTORING — restoring reintroduces two known-fatal failure modes.

0. WHY YOU PROBABLY SHOULD NOT RESTORE THIS. The dataflow was not retired for taste; it is incompatible with the SPN-driven CI/CD path. If you restore it, `fabric-cicd` will unbind its credential on every publish, and an SPN-triggered refresh will fail with `SPNBasedRefreshNotAllowed`. A restore only makes sense if you have ALSO solved dataflow ownership (Power BI REST `Default.Takeover` minted as the Fabric user, or an Erik-owned 'Save as' copy) or abandoned SPN-driven deploys. Neither was solved at retirement time.

1. COMMIT PIN. `commit_sha` is the commit IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the retirement commit — the last commit where the dataflow was live in main, per rules/feature-retirement.md Step 2. It was re-pinned from the snapshot-time HEAD (04ed718) to this value once the removal was actually ready to land; `git log 04ed718..e9f594e -- fabric/bronze_azureSQLdb2table.Dataflow/` is empty, so the two are equivalent as restore sources. Cherry-pick or copy from this SHA.

2. THE `CorrectedDate` LOGIC IS NOT IN THE SNAPSHOT ALONE — IT WAS MOVED, NOT DELETED. `#date(Date.Day([Date]) + 2000, Date.Month([Date]), Date.Year([Date]) - 2000)` (a day/year swap correcting malformed source dates) was relocated into `fabric/bronze-to-silver.Notebook/notebook-content.py`, with a mirror in `src/transformations/` and parity tests in `tests/` per the reference-implementation contract in root CLAUDE.md. A naive restore that puts the dataflow back WITHOUT removing the silver-side correction will apply the swap TWICE and silently corrupt every date. Remove the silver-side correction in the same change, and re-run the date-parity test.

3. FILTER-ORDER SEMANTICS — AND A TRAP. The mashup's incremental 7-day look-back (`WHERE Date >= '<p_from_date minus 7 days>'`) runs against the RAW, still-malformed `Date`, with the correction applied afterwards. If you restore and re-enable it, preserve that ordering — 'fixing' the filter to run on corrected dates changes which rows load. **BUT DO NOT ASSUME BRONZE INCREMENTAL LOADING EVER WORKED.** That look-back sat in the `else` branch of `if p_from_date = "1900-01-01" then <full table> else <native query>` (mashup.pq:9), and the pipeline's RefreshDataflow activity passed NO parameters — verify with `git show <pin>:fabric/orchestrator_pipeline_bronze_to_gold.DataPipeline/pipeline-content.json` and look at the `bronze_procurement` activity's typeProperties, which carry only dataflowId/workspaceId/notifyOption/dataflowType. So `p_from_date` always held its default, the else branch was UNREACHABLE, and bronze always full-loaded. The code is real; the behaviour was dead. Incrementality lives in the silver delete-insert window, not here.

4. `fabric/parameter.yml` HAS TWO REFERENCES, BOTH NEEDING WORK ON RESTORE. (a) A `key_value_replace` entry mapping `$.properties.activities[?(@.name=="bronze_procurement")].typeProperties.dataflowId` to `$items.Dataflow.bronze_azureSQLdb2table.$id` — removed when the Copy activities landed; must be re-added. (b) A `KNOWN LIMITATION — DATAFLOW CONNECTION RE-BINDING` comment block, rewritten at retirement. NOTE: that block was ALSO WRONG before the rewrite — it pointed at the tenant-level Settings -> Manage connections and gateways -> Data sources page. The Gen2 credential is NOT bound there and NOT in the source step's gear dialog; it is bound INSIDE THE DATAFLOW DEFINITION, which is exactly what the publish strips. Do not resurrect the old wording.

5. THE CAVEAT BLOCK STILL SERVES TWO LIVE ITEMS. `EPI_file2table` and `WGI_file2table` remain as Dataflow items and are still subject to the publish-unbinds-credentials gotcha, even though task-035 removed them from the pipeline's activity path. The re-bind guidance was narrowed, not deleted.

6. SPEC MARKERS TO REVERT — FOUR LOCATIONS, NOT ONE. spec_v1.md lines ~150 (Data Sources / Ingestion Method), ~628 (Orchestration Stage 1 activity table row 4), ~828 (Current State Assessment), ~991-993 (Naming Conventions / Dataflows). Each carries a `**Retired (2026-07-31)**` marker. Per DEC-016 all four route through `/iterate` — do NOT edit the spec inline.

7. UNMARKED MIRROR DOCS. `README.md` (lines ~31, ~64 incl. a mermaid node `B1[bronze_procurement]`) and `project_definition.md` (lines ~143, ~635-637, ~847, ~1039) also describe the dataflow. They are outside the spec, take no retirement marker, and were updated at retirement — check them on restore.

8. TEST FIXTURE. `tests/test_retry_ordinal.py:51` keys synthetic retry data on the activity name `"bronze_procurement"`. It is synthetic and does not read the dataflow, but the activity name changes with the Copy migration — check it.

9. APPLICATION STATE IS NOT IN THE SNAPSHOT. The dataflow wrote lakehouse tables `bronze_procurement_transactional` and `bronze_supplier_ref` in `oem_lh` (488fb9f8-e635-4683-90c4-ba4fee9dfadb, workspace 99e4cc6d-6ec3-49a7-aed9-b69b04a97aa9). Those are data, not code. The Copy activities write the SAME table names, so a restore does not need a table migration — but verify the schema, in particular that `Date` is the corrected column.

10. CREDENTIALS ARE NOT IN THE SNAPSHOT AND MUST NOT BE. The Azure SQL server admin login is `erikdatabase` (NOT `erikdatabase2`, a stale contained-DB user with a separate password that caused several failed re-bind attempts). The password lives in Erik's password manager only. A diagnostic firewall rule `erik-laptop` (37.247.31.201/32, dynamic) may still exist on server `procurement-supplier` in RG1.
